medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The School of Medicine believes that a vibrant and diverse institutional climate is essential in providing medical education that promotes the effective delivery of health care in diverse communities. A diverse learning environment includes people with various racial and ethnic origins, socioeconomic backgrounds, rural and urban communities, geographic origins and academic backgrounds. The Office of Inclusive Excellence promotes policies, initiatives and resources that create an environment of success for all, including students underrepresented in medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Many students enter the School of Medicine with extraordinary leadership experiences. As a UMKC School of Medicine student, one has the opportunity to get involved with more than 300 student organizations including Greek life, multicultural groups, honorary and service groups, religious organizations, service clubs and intramural sports. In addition, the School of Medicine has a variety of organizations to bring medical students together. These include the American Medical Association Student Chapter, the Medical Student Advisory Council, the Student National Medical Association, Alpha Omega Alpha, as well as many specialty interest groups. A complete listing of student organizations can be found at med.umkc.edu.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The UMKC School of Medicine has two locations: downtown Kansas City and St. Joseph. The KC campus is in close proximity to several of our partner hospitals: Truman Medical Center, Children's Mercy Hospital, and the Center for Behavioral Medicine. Located 50 minutes north of Kansas City, the St. Joseph Campus is in partnership with the Mosaic Life Center Hospital. By joining either campus, you will be located near cultural and entertainment districts such as the Country Club Plaza and the Power and Light District, as well as the Nelson Atkins Museum of Art, the Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts, the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum, the Jazz Museum and other great local and cultural activities in Kansas City. You will also be near all the vibrant events St. Joseph has to offer. Both locations provide excellent local flavor at some of our fabulous restaurants.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Students in year 1 of the B.A./M.D. program are required to live in residence halls available on the Volker campus, a campus located approximately 4 miles south of the Hospital Hill campus.  Students in year 2 can choose to remain in university housing on the Volker campus or can choose to move to off-campus housing.  University housing on the Hospital Hill campus available for upper-level students. Most students live in apartments or houses in the surrounding Kansas City area.

M.D. students in Kansas City are not required to live on campus but have the option to live in university housing located on the Health Science District campus. Most students live in apartments or houses in the surrounding Kansas City area. M.D. students in St. Joseph live in apartments or houses in St. Joseph or commute from communities in the Kansas City metropolitan area.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The School of Medicine believes that a vibrant and diverse institutional climate is essential to the medical education and work environment, both promoting a culture of inclusion and the ability to effectively deliver healthcare in diverse communities.  We want all faculty, staff, trainees, and students to feel safe, valued, and represented in the School of Medicine. As part of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) we value and address the importance of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in supporting the retention, persistence, and success of the historically marginalized (race and gender binary identities) and underrepresented populations (first generation college student, first generation medical student, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, differently abled, military, ethnicity, non-traditional students, age, socio-economic status and other identity intersections) in the UMKC School of Medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Students seeking academic accommodations may contact the UMKC Student Accessibility Services office to discuss their needs and coordinate appropriate accommodations. They can be reached at accessibility@umkc.edu or 816-235-5612.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
** The UMKC School of Medicine Wellness Program serves all UMKC School of Medicine students, including those in our MSA and MSB programs. **

In addition to the intellectual capacity for the sciences, medical school requires strong time-management skills, self-discipline, and responsibility. In a six-year program, these skills are even more imperative.

Change is not easy. All students should begin breaking down the areas of stress in their lives and coming up with feasible, measurable steps to achieve these skills early on in their academic careers.

An important key to developing as a student & a future physician is self-awareness.

Wellness Planning is a great way to do just that. As a service to you, the UMKC School of Medicine Wellness Program offers individual planning and coaching. The first session involves the Take Care of Yourself wellness inventory. This inventory will allow you to do the following:

Identify current stressors
Identify strengths
Identify areas for improvement
Create an action plan
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Our Kansas City campus has been training medical students for over 50 years at our community-based, affiliate institutions such as University Health, Children’s Mercy, and St. Luke’s. Learning communities led by physician mentors in primary care provide learning opportunities for students both in the in-patient and outpatient setting while providing continuity of care for patients. Set in the heart of Kansas City at our Health Sciences District location, our Kansas City campus students learn alongside students training in other health careers such as physician assistants, anesthesiology assistants, nurses, dentists, and pharmacists. The School of Medicine building houses several lecture halls and classroom spaces, a library, simulation-based learning opportunities, research labs, and various administrative staff. Students admitted to the MD program will learn alongside students in our combined BA/MD degree program.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The curriculum in the medical school is consistently challenging, and students must investigate numerous study skills and methods to address these challenges.  Academic support is available to assist.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students participate on a docent team all years of the program, gaining early interaction with patients.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations take place the last two years of the program in addition to the docent team. Rotations take place throughout the greater Kansas City area and in St. Joseph.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The UMKC School of Medicine offers two programs leading to the Doctor of Medicine degree:  the six-year combined degree B.A./M.D. program and the M.D. program.

THE B.A./M.D. PROGRAM

The School of Medicine offers a year-round program leading to baccalaureate and M.D. degrees in six calendar years. The program is designed primarily for high school seniors entering college. To receive the baccalaureate degree, the student must complete 120 semester hours of credit and will earn degrees in liberal arts, biology or chemistry. Under the guidance of a clinician-scholar called a docent, small groups of first and second-year students are introduced to medicine in community hospitals where they can observe patients and their care. During the first two years of the program, the student is occupied predominantly with undergraduate coursework, with about one-fourth of the time being devoted to introduction to medicine courses. medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
THE B.A./M.D. PROGRAM

For students in the B.A./M.D. program, the following components of the curriculum are designed to introduce students to primary care: in year one of the program, students are assigned to weekly experiences with physicians in the community, including family physicians, pediatricians, and internists. In years 3 -6, students are required to complete a clerkship in Family Medicine and a rural Missouri preceptorship. In addition, students spend a half-day a week every week for the last four years of the program working in an internal medicine clinic in one of two of our partner hospitals.

THE MD PROGRAM

Students in the MD program are required to complete a clerkship in Family Medicine and a rural Missouri preceptorship. In addition, students spend a half-day a week every week throughout the program working in an internal medicine clinic in one of our partner hospitals.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students have the opportunity to work with faculty in both clinical and research settings.  Students participating in research have received fellowships with nationally recognized research institutions such as the National Institutes of Health and the Doris Duke Charitable Foundation.  The Office of Research oversees the Student Research Program that supports student research efforts as well as coordinates supplemental research lectures and seminars.  Students involved in research projects have opportunities to present their findings to colleagues across campus and across the country.  Students have the opportunity to participate in research at the both the undergraduate and professional level.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Semester-based for the first 2 years (BAMD); 11 months of coursework (4-week block schedule) with 1 month vacation (MD)
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Truman Medical Center, St. Luke's Hospital, Children's Mercy, Center for Behavioral Medicine, Research Medical Center, Kansas City Veterans Affairs Med Center, and Mosaic Life Center Hospital

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Both the history and the current mission and operations of the UMKC School of Medicine are deeply rooted in the community at the local, state, national and international levels. As part of a growing academic health sciences campus in Kansas City, MO, and at a new campus in St. Joseph, MO, the School advances the health of the community through education of physicians, through research and application of new knowledge to health conditions that affect our community, through direct service in the community, and through economic development. In the nearly four decades that the School has been in existence, all of the four mission areas—education, research, service, and economic development—have grown and matured with the Health Sciences District. The University of Missouri-Kansas City is a public, urban, research and doctoral university. The campus in Kansas City serves the surrounding urban community, and the St. Joseph campus provides an opportunity to focus on rural healthcare.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The mission of the UMKC School of Medicine is to improve community health through:

Innovative educational programs in medicine and biomedical science
Cutting-edge biomedical research
Leadership in academic medicine

We strive to implement this mission with the highest professional and ethical standards, in a culture of inclusive excellence, and in an environment that enables individuals to reach their full potential.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege: Students complete the BA/MD degree across both of our downtown Kansas City campuses, the Volker campus and the Health Science District campus.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The BA/MD program is our foundational program at the UMKC School of Medicine. This program founded our school back in the early 1970's, and we have successfully been operating this program for over 50 years. As one of only two medical schools who offer this specific accelerated track, we accept 105 students a year into this program, the largest in the country. Students obtain six years of clinical exposure and experience, while balancing undergraduate and professional level medical school offerings.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: The School of Medicine participates in the AMCAS letter of recommendation program, and all letters of recommendation must be submitted through the AMCAS letter of recommendation service. Letters of recommendation sent directly to the School of Medicine will not be accepted or used in the admission process. It is recommended that letters come from those who can speak to your academic ability and other personal characteristics as they relate to medical school. Family members and/or friends of the family should not provide letters of recommendation. A minimum of three letters of recommendation is required. UMKC School of Medicine will accept committee letters completed by three of more individuals.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Step 1: American Medical College Application Service (AMCAS)
All applicants must apply through AMCAS. Please follow the instructions provided on the AMCAS application. Once the application has been verified by AMCAS, it will be sent to the medical schools to which you have applied. The AMCAS application must be submitted by July 1* and verified by August 1*. Official transcripts must be sent to AMCAS and received by July 15*. Any transcripts received after July 15 will not allow the AMCAS application to be processed. Letters of Recommendation must also be submitted through the AMCAS Letter of Recommendation Service by July 1*. Applications submitted to and verified by AMCAS earlier in the process will be reviewed first.

Transcripts
Official transcripts must be sent to AMCAS by July 15*. AMCAS will not transmit your application if transcripts are not received by July 15*. To prevent delays from occurring, you should use the AMCAS Transcript Request form when requesting that official transcripts be sent to AMCAS in support of your application. You can find this form in the Schools Attended section of the AMCAS application.

Letters of Recommendation
The School of Medicine participates in the AMCAS letter of recommendation program, and all letters of recommendation must be submitted through the AMCAS letter of recommendation service. Letters of recommendation sent directly to the School of Medicine will not be accepted or used in the admission process. It is recommended that letters come from those who can speak to your academic ability and other personal characteristics as they relate to medical school. Family members and/or friends of the family should not provide letters of recommendation. A minimum of three letters of recommendation is required. UMKC School of Medicine will accept committee letters completed by three of more individuals.

Official MCAT Scores
Applicants must sit for the MCAT by the end of July to guarantee an on-time review. For applicants selected for an interview, the August MCAT will be considered in the final review process.

Step 2: Secondary Application
All applicants must complete the secondary application, the General Application for Admission to UMKC. Applicants should not wait for a secondary invite in order to complete the General Application for Admission to UMKC. The application and $50 application fee must be submitted by August 8, 2026. For additional instructions, check out Steps for submitting the General App for the MD Only program.

Step 3: Supplemental Application (MD Student Portal)
All applicants must submit the School of Medicine Technical Standards. Applicants will receive a supplemental invite with information related to the electronic completion of the Technical Standards. Applicants will not receive the supplemental invite (UMKC MD portal) until after they have been verified by AMCAS. The deadline to submit is August 8, 2026. 

By receiving the supplemental invite, students will have access to the UMKC student portal. In the UMKC student portal, students must complete a final submission of the supplemental application. The final submission cannot be completed until the letters of reference, Technical Standards and General Application for Admission to UMKC have been processed and marked as complete. Applicants can only complete the final submission after all application components are marked as complete in the UMKC student portal under the Supplemental Application tab. Please note: It may take up to one week after submission of the General Application for Admission to UMKC before it is marked as complete.

medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept in-person and online courses in regard to our pre-requisites for our MD program, as long as you complete the courses from a regionally accredited and degree-awarding institution within the US.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: You will have the opportunity to review our technical standards when you complete and submit the MD secondary application. You will be required to read through and then sign and submit, to acknowledge you understand the technical standards.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The UMKC Student Financial Aid Office can assist with providing additional information regarding financial aid programs. The University participates in federal and state grant and loan programs, and need-based scholarships may also be available to students who qualify. In addition, the Financial Aid Office can offer more information on the types of expenses to expect, as well as the type of assistance that may be available. For additional information related to costs and financial assistance, please contact: Student Financial Aid office, UMKC, 5115 Oak Street, Kansas City, Missouri, 64110. The School of Medicine also offers the assistance of a Financial Literacy Counselor, who offers financial literacy training as well as other services. The Financial Literacy Counselor can be reached at 816-235-1870 or medicine@umkc.edu.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants may be placed on a waitlist for admission. If a position in the class becomes available, an offer of admission may be made to the next candidate on the waitlist.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Applicants must:

Have earned, or will soon earn, a baccalaureate, masters, or doctoral degree awarded from a regionally-accredited college or university in the United States.

Earned a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (GPA of 3.5 if not a resident of Missouri, Arkansas, Illinois, Kansas, Nebraska, or Oklahoma).

Earned a minimum GPA of 3.0 in the AMCAS BCPM (Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics coursework). (GPA of 3.5 if not a resident of Missouri, Arkansas, Illinois, Kansas, Nebraska, or Oklahoma).

Completed the following pre-requisite courses with a grade of B or better:
One semester of biochemistry (upper level course)
One semester of genetics
One semester of cell biology

These courses must be completed at a regionally accredited college or university located in the United States.

(Applicants to the B.A./M.D. Program are not required to have completed college coursework at the time of application.)
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: All applications to UMKC's School of Medicine are considered equally in the admissions process. All applications are initially screened by members of the Council on Selection. All applications are screened in the same applicant pool, and the screening process determines which students will be offered the opportunity to interview. Once interviews are complete, all interviewed applicants are reviewed equally by members of the Council. The Council considers each applicant individually within the appropriate applicant pool, and all applicants are reviewed under the same criteria and expectations. The selection process provides individual review of applicants in both the screening and selection process, competitive review of all applicants and does not adhere to strict requirements or standards as the review of applicants is holistic. The School of Medicine does not adhere to any quotas when considering and selecting students for admission to medical school.
